skill.name: momentic-result-classification
skill.description: Classify or explain Momentic test run results using Momentic MCP tools. Use when the user asks to categorize a failure, understand why a run failed, triage test results, or compare run results to past run results.
skill.summary: Investigate Momentic test runs, identify root causes, and assign evidence-based failure classifications.
skill.author: momentic-ai

security_audit.summary: All 58 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, ordinary test-analysis prose, and a documented Momentic run-link template. The skill uses expected Momentic MCP tools, and no command execution, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or unauthorized network behavior is present.

content.value_statement: Test failures can hide their true cause behind later errors or retries. This skill investigates Momentic run evidence and produces a precise classification.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the earliest step or container where a Momentic run entered an incorrect state.
Compares screenshots, traces, URLs, DOM data, and recovery logs to establish a root cause.
Compares current results with relevant past runs and earlier attempts.
Assigns one supported failure category and one recoverability value.
Records a completed classification through the Momentic MCP tool when requested.
Produces concise reasoning with evidence references and a confidence level.
limitations: Requires access to Momentic MCP tools and the relevant test run data.
Cannot prove a cause when screenshots, traces, or step results are missing or ambiguous.
Does not repair application code, infrastructure, or test definitions.
Historical comparisons may be misleading when branches or test definitions differ.

use_cases.title: Triage a failed test run
use_cases.description: Find the earliest divergence and classify the failure using direct run evidence.

use_cases.title: Investigate intermittent failures
use_cases.description: Compare attempts and past runs to distinguish consistent defects from temporary conditions.

use_cases.title: Review release test failures
use_cases.description: Summarize root causes, recoverability, and confidence for failed end-to-end checks.

prompt_templates.title: Classify one failed run
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate Momentic run [run ID]. Identify the earliest divergence, classify the failure, determine recoverability, and explain the evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a single failed test run.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain why Momentic run [run ID] failed. Trace backward from the final error and cite the screenshots, URLs, or step results that prove the cause.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a clear root-cause explanation is more important than history.

prompt_templates.title: Compare with previous runs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Momentic run [current run ID] with relevant earlier runs on the same branch. Determine what changed and provide the formal classification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a prior passing run may clarify the failure.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze retries and recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze every attempt and recovered child step in Momentic run [run ID]. Identify hidden partial failures, broken postconditions, category, recoverability, and confidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for complex runs with retries, modules, or recovery behavior.

output_examples.input: Classify a run where a row action succeeded, but the expected editor never opened.
output_examples.output: Reasoning: The row action was the earliest divergence. The screenshot stayed on the parent page, so the later title assertion checked unrelated text. Category: BUG. Recoverable: NON_RECOVERABLE. Confidence: high.

output_examples.input: Review a run where a broad text assertion passed before typing occurred in the wrong field.
output_examples.output: Reasoning: The assertion did not prove the intended page state. A more specific assertion and target can prevent recurrence. Category: TEST_AUTHORSHIP. Recoverable: RECOVERABLE. Confidence: high.

output_examples.input: Explain a run that failed because a required upload file was unavailable.
output_examples.output: Reasoning: The required file was missing before the picker action, and the test cannot create it. Category: TEST_SETUP. Recoverable: NON_RECOVERABLE. Confidence: high.

best_practices: Inspect the current run before using historical results.
Verify causal claims with screenshots, step results, URLs, DOM data, or traces.
Match past runs by branch and test version whenever possible.
anti_patterns: Do not classify only from the final failing assertion.
Do not label a single failure as flaky without comparable evidence.
Do not infer overlays, page states, or application changes without direct evidence.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a Momentic run identifier or supplied run details, plus access to relevant Momentic MCP tools.

faq.question: Can it compare previous runs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect relevant earlier runs, attempts, screenshots, and matching step results.

faq.question: Does it automatically save the classification?
faq.answer: It can submit the final classification through Momentic after the investigation is complete.

faq.question: Can it identify flaky tests?
faq.answer: It can identify intermittent behavior only when comparable runs show the same test and application behavior.

faq.question: What categories can it return?
faq.answer: It uses the categories defined by Momentic, including application changes, bugs, test authorship, setup, infrastructure, Momentic issues, and other.

faq.question: Can it fix the failed test?
faq.answer: No. It can explain whether a test update may recover the failure, but it does not edit tests or application code.
